system_description.narrative_title: Hormuz negotiations amid Iran threats, attacks and oil-market volatility
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that Iran and Oman are negotiating passage arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz while concurrent Iranian threats, missile strikes on shipping, and U.S. diplomatic signaling (including from President Trump) keep the region and oil markets highly volatile. As an open system this combines flows of energy (oil exports, shipping traffic), information and diplomacy (talks, public statements), coercive force (missile strikes, naval posture) and economic signals (oil prices, trading bets, sanctions), with feedback loops where incidents escalate insecurity and price moves, and market/financial reactions in turn shape political and military choices.
system_description.scope: Negotiations over Strait of Hormuz transit and coordinates; Iran, Oman, Gulf states (UAE, Saudi, Bahrain, others); U.S. administration and statements by President Trump; naval incidents and missile attacks (including Houthis); global oil exports and shipping routes; markets (oil futures, traders), sanctions and financial actions affecting Iran.
system_description.super_system: Global energy security and international geopolitical stability (global oil trade and strategic maritime chokepoints)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and commodity trading
U.S. domestic politics and presidential diplomacy
Regional military/naval operations and defense pacts in the Gulf
International shipping, maritime insurance and logistics
evidence_headlines: Iran, Oman say Strait of Hormuz talks in final stages, as Trump again teases a deal being close
EXCLUSIVE: Iran warns Gulf states: tell Trump to desist or we hit you hard

variables.name: Maritime traffic volume
variables.description: The aggregate throughput of commercial and cargo vessels transiting the strategic waterway over time.

variables.name: Energy export volume
variables.description: The quantity of hydrocarbon exports (oil, refined products, gas) moving through or originating in the region per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime security risk
variables.description: The perceived and measured level of threat to commercial shipping from hostile actions, mines, or accidents in the maritime domain.

variables.name: Military coercion level
variables.description: The intensity and readiness of coercive military posturing, threats, and deployments affecting the corridor.

variables.name: Attack incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of kinetic attacks, missile strikes, interdictions or hostile engagements affecting vessels or infrastructure.

variables.name: Naval deployment density
variables.description: The aggregate concentration of naval and coercive maritime assets present in and around the chokepoint.

variables.name: Negotiation intensity
variables.description: The tempo, frequency and resource commitment to diplomatic talks and bargaining over passage arrangements.

variables.name: Deal closure likelihood
variables.description: The perceived probability that formalized transit arrangements or agreements will be concluded and adopted.

variables.name: Shipping route control
variables.description: The degree to which any actor or mechanism can direct, restrict, or enforce the permitted trajectories of commercial shipping.

variables.name: Speculative positions
variables.description: The aggregate size and direction of speculative financial positions betting on energy prices and related risks.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of fluctuations in benchmark energy prices driven by perceived supply and geopolitical risk.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure
variables.description: The intensity and scope of economic and financial restrictions deployed to influence actors connected to the corridor.

variables.name: Liquidity constraints
variables.description: The degree to which financial access, banking services and asset mobility are restricted for regional actors.

variables.name: Signal clarity
variables.description: The clarity, consistency and credibility of public statements and communications about intentions and arrangements.

variables.name: Shipping insurance costs
variables.description: The market price of insuring vessels and cargoes against war, piracy and political risks in the corridor.

variables.name: Diplomatic trust level
variables.description: The underlying level of mutual confidence between negotiating parties that commitments will be honored and enforced.

catalysts.title: Imminent Iran–Oman Strait of Hormuz deal
catalysts.description: Finalized agreement between Iran and Oman to define/reopen a transit corridor and coordinates through the Strait, potentially formalizing control terms.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'talks in final stages', 'reached agreement with Oman', 'US expects deal soon', 'would give Iran control'.

catalysts.title: Continued missile and tanker attacks in Gulf
catalysts.description: Ongoing missile strikes and proxy attacks on tankers/ships in and near Hormuz/Red Sea, sustaining kinetic threats to commercial shipping.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iranian missile targets UAE tanker', 'UAE says ship targeted', 'Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil tankers'.

catalysts.title: Iranian parliamentary push to bar US/Israeli ships
catalysts.description: Parliamentary committee reviewing a draft bill to prohibit US and Israeli naval passage through Hormuz, potentially codifying restrictions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'parliamentary committee reviews draft bill to bar US, Israeli ships from Hormuz.'

catalysts.title: Sunni defense pact spurs coordinated naval deployments
catalysts.description: New Sunni defense pact triggers joint patrols/deployments aimed at securing shipping lanes and deterring attacks around Hormuz.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Sunni powers sign defense pact'; 'US expects deal soon as Sunni powers sign defense pact.'

catalysts.title: Shipping industry refuses proposed Hormuz passage
catalysts.description: Major carriers and insurers declare the proposed controlled-route infeasible and continue rerouting or avoidance, undermining practical reopening.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Proposed Hormuz passage deal not feasible for shipping industry'; 'Vessel traffic through Hormuz dwindles.'

catalysts.title: Expanded sanctions and financial freezes targeting Iran-linked entities
catalysts.description: New and rolling sanctions, asset freezes and penalties (banks, exchanges) restrict Iran-linked financial flows and intermediaries used for oil trade.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US sanctions Dubai crypto exchange', 'Iran state oil company's bank accounts frozen.'

catalysts.title: Continued idling of Kharg Island and stalled Iranian exports
catalysts.description: Kharg Island remains idled and Iran's crude exports stay constrained under blockade and operational disruptions, keeping supply suppressed.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran’s oil exports stall and Kharg Island idles under US blockade.'
